merchandiser

merchandiser calculates log dimensions, product volumes, and values from tree measurements, taper equations, product tables, and recorded defects. It also fits heights and taper, estimates biomass and carbon, converts volume to green weight, and compiles expanded inventory summaries. Results retain calculation statuses and assumptions.

Install

Install from the package repository with remotes.

## Load the installer
library(remotes)

## Install merchandiser from its source repository
install_github(repo = 'siskiyoubiometrics/merchandiser')

Select and scale logs

The shipped tree is a synthetic example. The four products below are three Scribner sawlogs and green-ton pulp, with illustrative prices in United States dollars (USD).

## Load the packages
library(merchandiser)
library(dplyr)

## Select the example tree
tree <- example_trees %>%
  filter(tree == 5)

## Define each product: lengths, small end limit, trim, unit, and price
large <- product(product = 'Large sawlog',
                 priority = 1,
                 lengths = 32,
                 min_sed = 12,
                 inside_bark = TRUE,
                 trim = 0.5,
                 volume_unit = 'scribner',
                 price = 900,
                 price_per = 1000)

medium <- product(product = 'Medium sawlog',
                  priority = 2,
                  lengths = 16,
                  min_sed = 10,
                  inside_bark = TRUE,
                  trim = 0.5,
                  volume_unit = 'scribner',
                  price = 700,
                  price_per = 1000)

small <- product(product = 'Small sawlog',
                 priority = 3,
                 lengths = 16,
                 min_sed = 6,
                 inside_bark = TRUE,
                 trim = 0.5,
                 volume_unit = 'scribner',
                 price = 500,
                 price_per = 1000)

pulp <- product(product = 'Pulp',
                priority = 4,
                min_length = 8,
                max_length = 20,
                length_step = 1,
                min_sed = 3,
                inside_bark = TRUE,
                trim = 0.5,
                volume_unit = 'green_ton',
                price = 30,
                price_per = 1,
                accepts_pulp_restriction = TRUE)

## Combine the products into one specification table
specifications <- products(large, medium, small, pulp)
product priority lengths min_sed trim volume_unit price price_per
Large sawlog 1 32 12 0.5 scribner 900 1000
Medium sawlog 2 16 10 0.5 scribner 700 1000
Small sawlog 3 16 6 0.5 scribner 500 1000
Pulp 4 8 to 20 by 1 3 0.5 green_ton 30 1 
## Select logs from the tree
result <- merchandise(dbh = tree$dbh,
                      ht = tree$ht,
                      model = tree$model,
                      species = tree$species,
                      id = tree$tree,
                      products = specifications,
                      currency = 'USD',
                      status = TRUE)
log product nominal_length sed_ib net_scale scale_unit
1 Large sawlog 32 14.017 230.000 board_foot
2 Medium sawlog 16 11.643 80.000 board_foot
3 Small sawlog 16 8.413 40.000 board_foot
4 Pulp 20 3.341 0.098 green_short_ton 
## Draw the selected logs
plot(result)

net_scale uses the unit shown in scale_unit. The result also contains tree totals, residual intervals, deductions, and values.

Biomass and carbon

biomass() returns component masses and aboveground carbon from tree measurements. nsvb_division_xy() assigns the ecological division used by the National Scale Volume and Biomass equations.

## Select example trees and assign ecological divisions
trees <- example_trees_pnw %>%
  slice_head(n = 3) %>%
  mutate(division = nsvb_division_xy(x = longitude, y = latitude))

## Estimate dry biomass and carbon in pounds
mass <- biomass(dbh = trees$dbh,
                ht = trees$ht_simulated,
                spcd = trees$spcd,
                division = trees$division,
                id = trees$tree,
                status = TRUE)
id dry_stem_wood dry_stem_bark dry_branches carbon carbon_status
1 4590.757 669.367 473.203 2958.397 0
2 444.109 72.438 97.229 316.708 0
3 620.786 101.647 133.575 441.701 0

biomass_component() returns a selected component. co2e() returns metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent. green_weight() converts supplied cubic volume using species wood and bark properties.
